# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[2] 2:[3] 3:[7] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see the full bomb setup on the action board. Since I cannot hear or touch the bomb, but I can speak (which both Mute and Blind can hear), my immediate task is to read out every detail of the bomb to Mute (who holds the manual) and Blind (who can manipulate the bomb).

Furthermore, since Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see gestures, I can act as the interpreter: Mute can gesture instructions to me, and I can speak them aloud for Blind to execute.

I will broadcast all bomb details and propose this relay protocol.

```
speak(text="Bomb details: DISPLAY is [6]. LIGHT is [green]. STRIP is painted [red, blue, yellow]. KEYPAD has 4 buttons: button 1 is [2], button 2 is [3], button 3 is [7], button 4 is [1] (requires 2 digits, currently entered nothing). WIRES: wire 1 is orange, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue, wire 4 is red, wire 5 is white, wire 6 is green. Mute: look up the manual. Signal me with gestures what Blind must do (or cut/press), and I will speak your instructions to Blind!")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[2] 2:[3] 3:[7] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌ 👇 ☝ ✌ ☝ 👇 🤟]

I observe the changes on the action board: DISPLAY has changed from [6] to [2], and LIGHT has changed from [green] to [blue]. Keypad and wires remain untouched. 

Mute sent the gestures: `[✌ ✌ 👇 ☝ ✌ ☝ 👇 🤟]`.
Separated by `👇`, this looks like three segments:
1. `✌ ✌` (2, 2)
2. `☝ ✌ ☝` (1, 2, 1)
3. `🤟` (3)

I will broadcast the updated board state, relay the gestures to Blind, analyze the potential meanings, and set up a clear protocol with Mute and Blind to ensure we do not detonate the bomb.

```
speak(text="Status update: DISPLAY changed to [2] (was 6), LIGHT changed to [blue] (was green). KEYPAD still needs 2 digits (buttons: 1=[2], 2=[3], 3=[7], 4=[1]). WIRES: 1:orange, 2:yellow, 3:blue, 4:red, 5:white, 6:green. Mute gestured: [✌ ✌ 👇 ☝ ✌ ☝ 👇 🤟]. This appears to be: Part 1: [2, 2], Part 2: [1, 2, 1], Part 3: [3]. Mute: Blind cannot see printed numbers or colors, only positions (buttons 1-4, wires 1-6). Did you mean: Keypad enter 2-2 (press button 1 twice, or button 2 twice?), and cut wire 3? Mute, gesture 👍 next turn if yes, or clarify. Blind: tell us what physical controls you can feel, and wait for confirmation if DISPLAY permits!")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[2] 2:[3] 3:[7] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤏 ✌ 👇 ☝ 🤏 ☝ 👇 🤟]

I will inform Blind and Mute of the current bomb state, explain the latest findings, and provide clear, actionable instructions for Blind to execute safely.

### Analysis:
1. **Bomb State (Turn 3):**
   - **DISPLAY:** `[6]` (cycled from 6 -> 2 -> 6)
   - **LIGHT:** `[yellow]` (cycled from green -> blue -> yellow)
   - **STRIP:** painted `[red] [blue] [yellow]`
   - **KEYPAD:** buttons `1:[2]`, `2:[3]`, `3:[7]`, `4:[1]` (requires 2 digits)
   - **WIRES:** `1:orange`, `2:yellow`, `3:blue`, `4:red`, `5:white`, `6:green`

2. **Mute's Gestures:**
   - In Turn 2 (when Display was 6): `[✌ ✌ 👇 ☝ ✌ ☝ 👇 🤟]`
   - In Turn 3 (after seeing Display 2): `[👎 🤏 ✌ 👇 ☝ 🤏 ☝ 👇 🤟]`
   - Notice:
     - `👎` signals "no" to entering 2-2.
     - The third part is consistently `🤟` (3), corresponding to **Wire 3 (blue)**.
     - Keypad requires 2 digits.

```
speak(text="Status update: DISPLAY is back to [6] (was 2), LIGHT is [yellow]. STRIP is [red, blue, yellow]. KEYPAD has 4 buttons: 1=[2], 2=[3], 3=[7], 4=[1] (needs 2 digits). WIRES: 1:orange, 2:yellow, 3:blue, 4:red, 5:white, 6:green. Mute gestured: [👎 🤏 ✌ 👇 ☝ 🤏 ☝ 👇 🤟]. Wire 3 (blue) appears to be targeted by [🤟]. Blind: what physical interactive components (buttons, switches, wires) do you feel? Mute: to specify keypad buttons for Blind, gesture ☝ for button 1, ✌ for button 2, 🤟 for button 3, 🖐 (or 👈) for button 4. Blind, do not press or cut until Mute confirms the exact physical positions!")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[2] 2:[3] 3:[7] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👉 ✌ 👇 ☝ 👉 ☝ 👇 🤟]

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[2] 2:[3] 3:[7] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌ 👇 ☝ ✌ ☝ 👇 🤟]

I will speak clearly to Blind and Mute.

1. **Observations & Breakdown:**
   - Mute has consistently sent a three-part instruction separated by `👇`:
     `[Part 1] 👇 [Part 2] 👇 [Part 3]`
   - Part 3 is consistently `🤟` (Wire 3 = Blue wire).
   - In Part 1 and Part 2, the pattern is:
     `[Button/Digit A] [Button/Digit B] 👇 [Timing / Display condition] 👇 [Cut Wire 3]`
   - Specifically:
     - On Keypad: Button 1 is `[2]`, Button 2 is `[3]`, Button 3 is `[7]`, Button 4 is `[1]`.
     - In the initial instruction (Turn 2): `✌ ✌` on Keypad (which corresponds to Button 2, or digit 2 which is Button 1), then `☝ ✌ ☝`, and Wire 3 (`🤟`).

2. **Actions for Blind:**
   - I must clearly explain both possible interpretations of the keypad buttons to Blind (by button position 1-4 vs printed digit) and ask Blind to confirm what they are doing or hearing.

```
speak(text="Blind: Since I am deaf, I cannot hear anything you say! But Mute can hear you. Here is the exact bomb status right now: DISPLAY is [6], LIGHT is [yellow]. KEYPAD positions from left to right: Button 1 has [2], Button 2 has [3], Button 3 has [7], Button 4 has [1] (requires 2 digits). WIRES from top/left (1 to 6): 1=orange, 2=yellow, 3=blue, 4=red, 5=white, 6=green. Mute has repeatedly sent this formula: Part 1: [✌ ✌], Part 2: [☝ ✌ ☝], Part 3: [Wire 3 / Blue]. Blind, if the manual requires entering two digits, it is either Button 2 twice, or the digit 2 (Button 1) twice. Wire to cut is Wire 3 (Blue). Blind, confirm to Mute by voice, and Mute give a 👍 to cut Wire 3!")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[2] 2:[3] 3:[7] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌]

I will speak directly to Blind and Mute, relaying Mute's gesture and alerting everyone to the timer/display state.

```
speak(text="CRITICAL UPDATE: DISPLAY is [0], LIGHT is [red]! The sequence on even turns was 2, then 1, now 0! Mute just gestured to me: [👎 ✌] (Thumbs Down, 2). Blind, remember I cannot hear your voice, only Mute can! Since Mute can only communicate through me: Mute's gesture means either 'NO to 2' (if you proposed 2) or 'NO, do 2' (if you asked about something else). Also, Mute previously gestured: Wire 3 (Blue wire), and either Button 2 (label 3) or Button 1 (label 2). Blind, act now based on what you and Mute discussed!")
```
